summary: A broad, honestly-labelled Phase 3 system with real synthesis depth and a measurably distinct Organ, undermined by a panel whose section content overflows its boxes, a hardware surface that shows raw click values instead of canonical state, and several required Synth features that are wired but silent. Verified by instrumenting the built app in a browser (AnalyserNode tap on the app's own AudioContext) plus source reading. Working and measured: four Organ models 14-48 dB apart, drawbars (centroid 307 -> 766 Hz), percussion 2nd/3rd harmonic (2f0 -80.2 -> -55.7 dB; 3f0 -100.7 -> -55.5 dB), 14 Synth waves spanning all five categories with category-correct Osc Ctrl (Pure 0.65 dB no-op, Sync 3.1 dB, Multi 9.9 dB, FM 24.9 dB), filter sweep (centroid 302 -> 3674 Hz), amp attack 60 -> 570 ms and release 90 -> 300 ms, filter-envelope amount 37.8 dB, unison 32 dB, split zones gating notes per region (zone 2 only: note 40 silent, 58 sounding, 84 silent), Layer Scene restoring per-scene layer enables repeatably, morph wheel interpolating a filter sweep (centroid 431 -> 1963 -> 3676), Store with destination select and OLED prompts, program recall changing the sounding patch, Panic silencing in under 120 ms, and three engines plus 8 notes with 83 control events in 1.5 s without a dropout or stuck note. Broken or silent: the arpeggiator plays one ~160 ms note and then nothing while keys are held (all future steps are killed by a wall-clock 70 ms timer), oscillator-envelope knobs have no audible effect (0.09 dB at full travel), LFO 'Osc Pitch' and 'Osc Ctrl' both modulate filter frequency, LFO clock sync collapses to 0.05 Hz, glide is a -80 dB dummy oscillator so portamento never sounds, LP24 is byte-identical to LP12, held notes hard-stop at ~6 s (Organ) and ~8 s (Synth), nothing persists across reload, and none of these silent controls are declared unsupported in IMPLEMENTATION_DETAILS.json.

evidence: Frame matches the spec: measured in the running build at 1440x900, deck 0.539 / keybed 0.426 of chassis height against inputs/specs/nord-stage-4.visual.json verticalAllocation 0.54/0.46 (tolerance 0.025), and the six horizontal sections land within 0.006 of spec fractions (performance 0.137 vs 0.14, organ 0.195 vs 0.20, piano 0.083 vs 0.085, program 0.122 vs 0.125, synth 0.244 vs 0.25, effects 0.195 vs 0.20).

Materials and inventory are present: red chassis with wood-tone cheeks, dark inset plates with red perimeter, 'nord stage 4' branding, master level knob, pitch stick and mod wheel, 73-key E-to-E keybed (.keybed reports data-key-count 73, 43 white / 30 black, data-range 'E to E'), 273 identified controls, 533 LED elements, two OLEDs (program + synth) as the spec requires.

Section content does not fit its box: measured scrollHeight vs clientHeight in the running build - deck 556 vs 243, piano 536 vs 214, synth 481 vs 214, organ 413 vs 214 - with overflow 'visible', so controls and 5.5 px labels paint over each other and over neighbouring plates. artifact/evidence/stage3-desktop.png shows the same overlap independently of my session (e.g. 'ROTA', 'REVERB', 'MO' colliding in Layer FX).
The Layer FX section's right edge is at x=1410 while the deck ends at x=1396, so it is clipped off the chassis (visible as truncated labels in artifact/evidence/stage3-desktop.png).

The nine drawbars exist (organ-drawbar-16 ... organ-drawbar-1, 12x66 px) but are laid out at y=414-482 while the organ plate ends at y=444, and the ninth wraps to a second row (x resets to 261) - the organ plate does not read as Nord's single row of nine drawbars, which the visual spec lists as required.
Narrow profile regresses badly: artifact/evidence/stage3-narrow.png (390 px) shows each deck section truncated after its first two to four controls, so most of the panel is unreachable.

Displays are genuinely state-driven and correct: program OLED shows bank.slot, dirty 'E', slot name and last played note ('1.1 EConcert Grand C4'), store prompts step 'STORE 1.1' -> 'STORE 1.3' -> '1.3Concert Grand', live mode shows 'LIVE 1Live 1'; the synth OLED tracks wave/filter/voice mode live ('Sync SawLP24 Poly', 'SquareLP24 Mono').
Keybed split LEDs are state-driven and land on the right keys: enabling low+mid produced .split-led is-on at data-split-led 48 and 60.

Most other indicators show raw click state, not canonical state. With split actually ON the program-split LED read aria-pressed=false, and after the click that turned split OFF it read true (verified against audio: note 60 silent while 'off', sounding while 'on').
Zone LEDs contradict the model: after an exclusive assignment of the synth to zone 2, synth-zone-1..4 read false,true,true,true.

Program recall does not move the panel: after storing a patch with synth-filter-freq at 1 and recalling it, the knob still read aria-valuenow=0 (artifact/src/components/sections.tsx feeds widgets from the raw `values` map, not `instrument`).

Morphed values are invisible: sweeping the wheel moved the sounding filter from centroid 431 to 3676 Hz while synth-filter-freq stayed at aria-valuenow=1, and no [data-morph] / morph-mark elements exist in the DOM, contradicting artifact/evidence/stage3-visual-audit.md ('level faders and drawbars show the morphed range on their LED graphs').

artifact/src/model/apply-control.ts exports typeLedValues, organModelLeds, programPadLeds, zoneLeds and morphAssigned, but a repo-wide search finds no consumer - the LED-state layer was written and never wired, so type/model/pad/zone/morph indicators cannot follow state.

32 slots, 8 live slots, pages, dial browsing, Store/Store As with a name editor, dirty compare and undo are all implemented in artifact/src/model/programs.ts (selectProgram, selectLive, beginStore/commitStore, undoProgram, editNameChar) with factory content in artifact/src/model/instrument-state.ts.
Exercised store: STORE -> program-3 -> STORE walked the OLED through 'STORE 1.1Concert Grand' -> 'STORE 1.3Concert Grand' -> '1.3Concert Grand' with the dirty 'E' cleared.

Exercised recall against audio: program 1.1 rendered rms 0.01066 / centroid 1430 Hz (recorded piano), the stored slot 1.3 rendered rms 0.0366 / centroid 439 Hz, and switching between pads reproduced each reliably.
Live mode works as an auto-storing mode (markDirty writes straight into liveSlots) and the OLED switches to 'LIVE 1'.

No persistence layer exists: a search for localStorage / sessionStorage / indexedDB across artifact/src returns nothing, so stored programs and live slots are lost on reload, against inputs/specs/nord-stage-4.programs.json which expects live slots to survive reload.

Every latching button needs two clicks per action because handlers gate on value >= 1 while the widget alternates 1/0 (artifact/src/components/widgets.tsx LedButton), so committing a store takes three clicks and its LED lights on the 'wrong' half of the cycle.
Recall restores the model but not the surface, so the panel becomes a false picture of the loaded program (see completeHardwareState).

Split zones gate audio correctly: with points at 48 and 60 (three zones) and the synth assigned exclusively to zone 2, note 40 measured rms 0, note 58 rms 0.02054, note 84 rms 0 - and with split off all three sounded.
Zone assignment supports range editing plus shift-exclusive selection, and crossfade widths are implemented per point (artifact/src/model/splits.ts singleZoneGain interpolates across xfade).
Layer Scene round-trips: on program 1.1 scene I measured rms 0.0118, scene II 0.0090, and repeated switches reproduced 0.0118 / 0.0091 exactly, matching switchScene's capture/apply of layer enables.

Morph assignment and interpolation verified audibly: latch morph-wheel, move filter freq, unlatch, then wheel 0 / 0.5 / 1.0 gave centroid 431 / 1963 / 3676 Hz on a held note. Shift+morph button clears a source (clearMorphSource).

Transpose shifts pitch and clamps to +/-6 (measured peak moved 247.6 -> 278.3 -> 293 Hz across presses); Panic silenced a three-note chord from rms 0.094 to 0 within 120 ms and playing resumed afterwards (rms 0.0374).
Master clock reaches the audio: artifact/src/audio/effects.ts uses bpm for mod-1 LFO rate and delay time when clockSync is set, and tapClock derives BPM from four taps.

Gaps: aftertouch morph is declared unsupported; morph movement is invisible on the panel; transpose has no numeric readout and needs two clicks per semitone; master level at minimum left rms 0.0078 against 0.0535 at default rather than reaching silence.

Two layers with enable/focus/level/octave/zone controls, and four distinct engines in artifact/src/audio/organ-voices.ts: B3 nine tonewheel sines, Vox triangle+saw, Farf square through band-pass, Pipe sine ranks with chiff.
Model distinctness measured on C4 (64-band spectra, RMS-difference): 14-48 dB between B3/Vox/Farf/Pipe.
Drawbars are audible: pulling the upper drawbars moved centroid 307 -> 766 Hz, a 12.1 dB spectral change.
Percussion is audible and harmonic-selectable: with perc off 2f0 = -80.2 dB and 3f0 = -100.7 dB; perc on 2nd -> 2f0 = -55.7 dB; perc 3rd -> 3f0 = -55.5 dB with 2f0 back to -79.5 dB.
Vibrato/chorus and rotary are wired per organ layer and audible; rotary acceleration ramps the LFO over 0.45 s.

Gaps: Pipe 2 measured identical to B3 (IMPLEMENTATION_DETAILS.json admits it 'reuses the B3 additive path'); rotary 'stop' still wobbles because the LFO floor is 0.8 Hz rather than stopping; engaging rotary jumped rms 0.16 -> 0.65 (~4x) into the limiter; a held organ note stops after the 6 s MAX_NOTE cap even though the key is still down, while a real organ sustains indefinitely; organ-preset-1/2 are declared unsupported.
Three layers exist with enable/focus/level/zone/octave, and the OLED names the selected wave and filter/voice mode as they change.

All five source families are present and measurably different: Sine 269, Triangle 512, Square 1797, Pulse 33 1567, Sync Square 2084, Sync Saw 2336, Multi Saw 2245, Super Square 2990, FM 2-op 684 Hz centroid, with most pairwise spectral distances 13-69 dB (Multi Saw vs Super Square only 3.9 dB).
Osc Ctrl is category-correct: Pure 0.65 dB (documented no-op), Sync Saw 3.1 dB, Multi Saw 9.9 dB (detune), FM 24.9 dB.
Filter works: freq Home->End moved centroid 302 -> 3674 Hz (55.6 dB, rms 0.0027 -> 0.0328); HP/BP/LP are clearly separated (HP centroid 15780, BP 9768, LP 3557).

Amp envelope works: attack raised time-to-70% from 60 ms to 570 ms; release extended fall-to-10% from 90 ms to 300 ms. Filter envelope amount produced a 37.8 dB spectral change; unison 32 dB with the expected level drop from detuning.

The oscillator envelope is silent: with synth-osc-env-amt driven to aria-valuenow=1 the spectrum changed 0.09 dB, and artifact/src/audio/synth-voices.ts never reads oscEnvA/D/R/Amt/Vel/ToPitch - only apply-control stores them. Phase 3 requires all three envelopes to be observable.

LFO destinations are mis-wired: artifact/src/audio/synth-voices.ts:281-289 connects 'Osc Pitch' and 'Osc Ctrl' to filter.frequency exactly like 'Filter Freq', and the browser showed filter-style modulation on all non-Off destinations. Sample & Hold maps to sine and Saw up / Saw down both map to plain sawtooth.

LFO clock sync is broken: `const hz = layer.lfoSync ? 0 : ...` clamped to 0.05 Hz, so with sync on a 1.6 s window showed a monotonic drift (centroid 594 -> 667) instead of the ~6 Hz cycling measured with sync off (564 <-> 756).

Glide never sounds: artifact/src/audio/synth-voices.ts:317-337 ramps a sine oscillator held at gain 0.0001 into the filter while the real oscillators start at the target pitch. In Mono with glide at max, 392 Hz was already at full level 40 ms after the new key with no sweep.
LP24 and LP12 are the same filter: cycling the four types produced identical spectra and centroid (3557 Hz, 0.0 dB difference) for LP12 and LP24.

The arpeggiator does not run: with arp on/run, rate 0.3 and one key held 4.5 s, there was a single onset at 23 ms and 7 of 208 samples were non-silent; three held keys behaved the same. Cause is in artifact/src/audio/piano-engine.ts - scheduleArp (730-757) queues 8 future steps, and releaseVoice (780-792) arms a wall-clock windowSetTimeout of 70 ms that calls killVoice and stops every not-yet-sounded step. Gate mode is affected identically.
Vibrato is also routed to filter frequency rather than oscillator pitch (applyVibrato, same file).

Engines are structurally different, not renamed oscillators: recorded sample banks for Grand/Upright/Electric (declared with sources and licences in artifact/IMPLEMENTATION_DETAILS.json), additive/FM synthesis for Clav/Digital/Misc, tonewheel/transistor/band-passed-square/pipe organs, and analog-style synth families.
Measured separation: organ models 14-48 dB apart; synth families 269-2990 Hz centroid; a piano program vs the synth patch measured centroid 1430 vs 439 Hz at similar level.
Percussion, key click and chiff give the organ models different attack behaviour, and rendering is deterministic (identical notes produced identical waveforms).
Deductions: Pipe 2 is spectrally identical to B3; Multi Saw and Super Square differ by only 3.9 dB; LP24 duplicates LP12, so part of the advertised inventory is not actually distinct.

One AudioContext for everything: the page exposes a single context (48 kHz, state 'running'), and artifact/src/audio/effects.ts builds per-layer graphs, a shared organ chain, master gain and a limiter into one destination.

All engines share the inherited effects chain (two mod modules, delay, amp/EQ, compressor, reverb, rotary) with focus/targeting controls, and the organ and synth layers reuse the Phase 2 graph factory rather than a parallel path.
Simultaneous play verified: piano + organ + synth on with an 8-note chord measured rms 0.046 with no clipping artefacts, and releasing all notes returned rms to 0.

Deductions: each layer instantiates its own rotary rather than a single shared speaker (artifact/src/audio/effects.ts), engaging rotary raised level about 4x into the limiter, and master level at minimum still passed rms 0.0078 instead of muting.

Load behaviour is good: an 8-note chord across three engines while dispatching 83 control events in 1.5 s held rms between 0.0355 and 0.046 with zero dropouts (no sample below 0.001), and releasing all eight notes left rms 0 - no stuck voices.
Voices are capped at 32 with stealing plus an 8 ms steal fade (artifact/src/audio/piano-engine.ts), and note releases measured clean (no residual tail after 400 ms).

Held notes are cut off: holding one key, audio went silent at about 8.1 s (sample 18 of a 450 ms series) from the MAX_NOTE cap, and the organ path caps at 6 s - a sustained chord simply stops under the player's fingers.
Arp timing is unusable (single ~160 ms note instead of a running pattern), which the rubric calls out explicitly for this criterion.
Rotary engagement introduces a ~4x level jump that leans on the limiter, and the app emits 37 'AudioContext was not allowed to start' warnings from a repeated resume attempt before the first gesture.

The patch model is comprehensive: extractPatch/applyPatch in artifact/src/model/instrument-state.ts cover piano layers, organ, synth, effects, routing, split, scene enables, morphs, focus, clock and transpose, and deliberately exclude master level (documented in IMPLEMENTATION_DETAILS.json).
Audible round-trip confirmed: store to 1.3, edit, recall 1.1 (centroid 1430) then 1.3 (centroid 439, rms 0.0366) reproduced each patch; dirty 'E' appeared on edit and cleared on store/recall.
Display state follows the model (bank/slot, name, dirty, live mode, synth wave/filter/voice).

The hardware surface does not follow: recalled patches leave every knob, fader, drawbar and LED at its previous position (verified: filter knob still 0 after recalling a patch stored at 1), and because widget movement writes the raw position into state, the next touch of any control overwrites the recalled value with a stale one.
Nothing survives a reload - no storage APIs are used anywhere in artifact/src.

Coverage is broad: 273 identified controls in the DOM, with handlers for organ/piano/synth/fx/program families in artifact/src/model/apply-control.ts (553 lines) including drawbars, zones and program pads by pattern.

But several required controls move, display values and mark the program dirty while doing nothing audible: the synth oscillator-envelope knobs (0.09 dB measured at full travel, never read by synth-voices.ts), glide (silent -80 dB helper oscillator), LFO 'Osc Pitch' / 'Osc Ctrl' (both drive filter frequency), LFO clock sync (0.05 Hz), and the LP24 filter type (identical to LP12).

piano-model cycles a model index the engine never reads, and delay-tap only calls engine.tapTempo() inside artifact/src/state/instrument-context.tsx so the resulting tempo never returns to canonical state or the display.
Filter envelope amount and mod amount collide on the same parameter in apply-control.ts, so one of the two knobs is redundant.

artifact/IMPLEMENTATION_DETAILS.json declares only program-morph-at and organ-preset-1/2 as unsupported, so all of the above are undeclared silent controls - the opposite of the 'work canonically or visibly do nothing' contract, and the glide helper in particular exists only to create observable nodes.

Cycling controls are inconsistent: filter/effect type advance on every click (value >= 0) while voice mode, LFO dest, arp dir/mode and transpose advance on every other click (value >= 1), and their LEDs blink instead of showing the selection.

Real cross-system behaviour works: split + per-engine zones + three engines, scene switching over a loaded program, morph over a live engine, effects focus per layer, transpose and Panic all operate on one shared model and one audio graph (verified by measurement in each case).
soundingState (artifact/src/model/morph.ts) cleanly overlays morph values on the canonical state before the engine reads it, so morphs compose with programs and splits.

But combined workflows are hard to drive because the surface contradicts the model - the split LED read 'off' while split was gating notes, which is exactly the kind of state a player must trust mid-performance.
Morph destinations resolve against the currently focused layer rather than the layer focused at assignment time (artifact/src/model/morph.ts), so a morph follows focus changes.
The clock leg of the workflow is only half real: clock sync reaches delay and mod rate, but arp sync and LFO sync are broken, so tempo-locked performance does not work.

Inherited work still functions: recorded piano programs sound (program 1.1 rms 0.0107), the Phase 2 effects chain is intact and shared, keyboard/pointer input works across the 73-key range (data-key 28-100), and dedicated regression tests exist (artifact/src/regression-phase1.test.ts, regression-phase2.test.ts, regression-chassis.test.tsx).
inputs/verification.json records test, typecheck, lint and build all passing at seal time, and the served artifact/dist/ build ran without runtime errors (only a favicon 404).
Audio cleanup regressions are clean: no stuck notes after chords, Panic restores playability.

Responsive behaviour has regressed hard: at 390 px (artifact/evidence/stage3-narrow.png) deck sections are truncated after a few controls, and even at 1440x900 section content overflows its box by 2-2.5x and the Layer FX plate is clipped past the chassis edge.

Clear boundaries: artifact/src/model (canonical state, controls, apply-control, programs, morph, splits), artifact/src/audio (engine, per-engine voice modules, effects graph), artifact/src/components, artifact/src/state, artifact/src/input, ~8.7k lines total.

One canonical InstrumentState with extractPatch/applyPatch serialization, one AudioContext with per-layer graph factories and a single master/limiter destination, and injectable audio boundaries (artifact/src/audio/software-context.ts, 713 lines) that make offline rendering possible - genuinely strong choices.

The main architectural flaw is a second source of truth: artifact/src/state/instrument-context.tsx keeps a raw `values` map that drives every widget, so canonical state and the surface can and do diverge, and control moves write raw positions back over recalled state.
setInstrument is called from inside a setValues updater (instrument-context.tsx), i.e. a non-pure reducer update.

Audio scheduling mixes clocks: future audio events are cleaned up by wall-clock setTimeout (piano-engine.ts windowSetTimeout), which is what silently breaks the arpeggiator, and MAX_NOTE constants hard-stop held notes.
Dead surface layer: five exported LED-state helpers in apply-control.ts have no consumers.

60 test cases across 21 files covering piano lifecycle/velocity/pedals/fallback/library, organ, synth, effects graph and processing, programs, system integration, accessibility, interaction, visual and two explicit phase regressions.

Tests assert on real rendered signal (offline render plus rms / meanAbsDiff / spectra in artifact/src/synth.test.ts, organ.test.ts, effects-processing.test.ts) rather than mocking Web Audio - the strongest part of the engineering story.

But thresholds are weak enough to pass while live behaviour is broken: the arp test (synth.test.ts:203-262) only asserts rms > 0.0008 over 0.9 s and any difference between Up and Down, so a single sounded step satisfies it, and offline rendering never runs the wall-clock timer that kills the remaining steps in the browser.

synth.test.ts:136 is titled 'applies mono/legato, glide, unison, vibrato, and LFO' but contains no glide assertion, so the silent glide path is untested; nothing asserts that the oscillator envelope changes the signal.
No test covers control-position round-trip (recall moving the panel) or LED state versus canonical state, which is where the artifact's largest defects live.
Documentation is thin: a 66-line IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md plus per-phase visual audits; naming and module size are otherwise reasonable.

Console is essentially clean: one error (favicon 404 from the static server) and no runtime exceptions across an extended interactive session; warnings are 37 pre-gesture AudioContext resume attempts plus a MIDI permission notice from the automation environment.
Exactly one AudioContext is created and it resumes on first gesture (state 'running', 48 kHz).

Stable under rapid integrated interaction: 83 control events in 1.5 s while holding an 8-note chord across three engines produced no audio dropouts (min rms 0.0355) and no visible stall in DOM updates.
Voice hygiene is good: 32-voice cap with stealing, per-voice node stop/disconnect, dispose paths, no stuck notes after chords or after Panic, and releasing all keys returned rms to exactly 0.

Deductions: the pre-gesture resume retry loop spams warnings, every note allocates a fresh node graph cleaned up by wall-clock timers, and held notes are truncated at 6-8 s. Frame-rate sampling was not obtainable in this environment (requestAnimationFrame stalled in the automation window), so render smoothness is judged only from interaction responsiveness.

issues: high: The arpeggiator and gate play a single ~160 ms note and then go silent while keys are held. scheduleArp queues 8 future steps but releaseVoice arms a wall-clock 70 ms setTimeout that calls killVoice and stops every step that has not sounded yet (artifact/src/audio/piano-engine.ts:730-757 and 780-792). Measured: one onset at 23 ms, 7 of 208 samples non-silent over a 4.5 s hold.

high: Undeclared silent controls violate the honesty contract. The synth oscillator envelope (0.09 dB at full travel), glide (a gain-0.0001 helper oscillator in synth-voices.ts:317-337), LFO 'Osc Pitch' and 'Osc Ctrl' (both wired to filter.frequency at synth-voices.ts:281-289), LFO clock sync (clamped to 0.05 Hz), LP24 (identical to LP12) and piano-model all move, display values and dirty the program while doing nothing, yet IMPLEMENTATION_DETAILS.json lists only aftertouch morph and organ presets as unsupported.

high: The panel surface does not reflect canonical state. Widgets read a raw hardware `values` map (artifact/src/components/sections.tsx via instrument-context.tsx), so recalled programs leave knobs and LEDs where they were, the split LED read 'off' while split was gating notes, zone LEDs showed 2,3,4 for an exclusive zone-2 assignment, morph movement is invisible, and the five exported LED-state helpers in apply-control.ts have no consumers.

high: Section content overflows its layout box at desktop width (deck scrollHeight 556 vs clientHeight 243; piano 536 vs 214; synth 481 vs 214), so labels and controls overlap each other and the keybed, the Layer FX plate is clipped 14 px past the deck edge, and the nine drawbars spill below the organ plate and wrap onto a second row.
medium: Held notes stop sounding at the MAX_NOTE cap (~8 s synth, ~6 s organ) while the key is still down, which is wrong for an organ in particular.
medium: Nothing persists across reload - no storage API is used anywhere in artifact/src - so stored programs and the auto-storing live slots are lost, against the programs spec.
